tour.welcomeDescription: Welcome to the tutorial of Eurostat's Energy Prices visualisation Tool. This guided tour will show you the main ways of interacting with the tool.
tour.languageDescription: Use this option to change the language of the tool. It supports English, French, and German.
tour.menuDescription: In addition to the bar options, the tool contains a menu for additional features. Click on the menu icon to customize the chart. Click next to learn about the menu options.
tour.insightsDescription: Open a summary of the data shown in this view.
tour.shareDescription: If you find this visualisation tool useful, please show your support by sharing it with others on X, Facebook, email, and LinkedIn. Thank you!
tour.downloadDescription: Click here to download chart or data.
tour.toolDescription: The title and subtitle describe what you are looking at.
tour.replayDescription: Use this button whenever you want to see this tour again.
tour.contentDescription: The charts and data of the tool appear here.
tour.chartDescription: The height of these bars represents the prices that customers pay for gas or electricity. By clicking on them, you can further disaggregate them into sub-categories or explore other statistics such as time graphs, pie charts, or bar charts to compare different consumption levels for the selected country.
tour.tableDescription: Use this option to change the chart to a table format.
tour.orderDescription: Use this option to change the order of the chart elements.
tour.aggregatesDescription: Use this option to add or remove aggregates from the chart.
tour.componentsDescription: Use this option to change to components mode.
tour.detailsDescription: Use this option to see in details.
tour.embedDescription: Use this button to embed the chart in other tools or websites.
tour.countryDescription: Click on a bar to see the details of that country: its prices by consumption level, the parts of the price in a pie chart and how the price developed over time.
tour.decimalsDescription: Click here to change how many decimals the prices show: 4, 3, 2 or 1. Every chart, tooltip and table follows.
tour.timelineDescription: Choose the period of the chart on the timeline, or press play to see how the prices change from one period to the next.

iv.TITLE: Insights
iv.ERROR: Insights could not be loaded for the current selection.
iv.CALC_LATEST_PRICE: Latest Price: Eurostat published dataset • Semester Change: (P_S2 − P_S1) / P_S1 × 100 • YoY Change: (P_t − P_t-1y) / P_t-1y × 100
iv.CALC_EU_COMPARISON: EU Gap %: (P_focus − P_EU27) / P_EU27 × 100 • Country Rank: 1 + Count(P > P_focus) • Median Gap: (P_focus − Median) / Median × 100
iv.CALC_COUNTRY_COMPARISON: Price Gap: (P_A − P_B) / P_B × 100 • YoY Growth: YoY_A vs YoY_B • Main Driver: Max( |Component_A − Component_B| )
iv.CALC_HISTORICAL: Peak: Max(P_t) • Minimum: Min(P_t) • Percentile: (Count(P_hist < P_current) + 0.5 × Count(P_hist = P_current)) / N × 100
iv.CALC_DEVELOPMENT: Momentum: YoY_t − YoY_t-1 • 5Y CAGR: ((P_t / P_t-5y)^(1/5) − 1) × 100 • Volatility: Standard deviation of 10-semester returns
iv.CALC_COMPOSITION: Component Shares: Component_val / Total_price × 100 • Main Driver: Max( |Delta_Component| )
iv.CALC_EUROPE: Counts of rising/falling countries & Dispersion Change = (IQR_latest − IQR_prior) / IQR_prior × 100
iv.CALC_BAND: Band Premium = (P_band − P_ref) / P_ref × 100 • Spread = P_highestBand − P_lowestBand
iv.CALC_PROVENANCE: Status inspection ('p'/'e'), anomaly validation (P > 0, |YoY%| < 200%), and dataset mapping
iv.FISCAL_EFFECT: Fiscal effect on the annual change
iv.COST_DISCLAIMER: Indicative energy cost only based on average statistical unit price; actual bills depend on individual supplier offers, contracts, fixed charges, and location.
iv.DATASET_PRICE_NOTE: Prices & trends sourced from bi-annual level dataset
iv.DATASET_COMPONENT_NOTE: Component breakdown sourced from annual detailed dataset
iv.CONSUMER_QUALIFICATION_DESC: Household and non-household energy prices are collected under distinct Eurostat methodologies. Non-household prices exclude recoverable VAT and apply industrial consumption thresholds, whereas household prices include all non-refundable taxes. Direct cross-comparison between consumer groups is methodologically invalid.
iv.SAFEGUARD_OK: Safeguard check passed: Non-zero, non-negative, plausible price movement.
iv.STATUS_NORMAL: Final published figure (no provisional or estimated flags).
iv.WHAT_LATEST_PRICE: The official published unit energy price for the selected country, consumer group, and consumption band.
iv.WHAT_SEMESTER_CHANGE: Percentage price change relative to the preceding 6-month period (S1 vs S2).
iv.WHAT_YOY_CHANGE: Percentage price change relative to the same semester of the previous year.
iv.PURPOSE_YOY_CHANGE: Evaluates annual inflation/deflation rate eliminating seasonal effects.
iv.WHAT_EU_GAP: Percentage gap between focus country price and official weighted EU27 average.
iv.PURPOSE_EU_GAP: Measures national price competitiveness relative to the European benchmark.
iv.WHAT_RANK: Position of focus country ordered from highest (1) to lowest price among reporting countries.
iv.PURPOSE_RANK: Identifies national ranking in the European price hierarchy.
iv.WHAT_MEDIAN_GAP: Percentage price gap relative to the unweighted median country price.
iv.PURPOSE_MEDIAN_GAP: Compares focus country to the middle-performing European country.
iv.WHAT_HIST_MAX: The highest unit price recorded for the focus country over the full historical observation window.
iv.PURPOSE_HIST_MAX: Identifies peak energy cost periods and price ceiling bounds.
iv.WHAT_HIST_MIN: The lowest unit price recorded for the focus country over history.
iv.WHAT_HIST_PERCENTILE: Percentage of historical periods where price was lower than the current price.
iv.PURPOSE_HIST_PERCENTILE: Measures historical extremity of current price.
iv.WHAT_MOMENTUM: Classification of price growth rate acceleration or slowdown.
iv.PURPOSE_MOMENTUM: Detects changing price dynamics before trend reversals appear in annual numbers.
iv.WHAT_CAGR: Compound Annual Growth Rate over the last 2 or 5 years.
iv.PURPOSE_CAGR: Smooths short-term semester spikes to reveal long-term structural trend slope.
iv.WHAT_VOLATILITY: Standard deviation of semester-on-semester percentage returns over 10 semesters.
iv.PURPOSE_VOLATILITY: Quantifies price instability and consumer tariff uncertainty.
iv.WHAT_SEASONAL: Typical price premium between semester 1 (S1) and semester 2 (S2) across historical years.
iv.PURPOSE_SEASONAL: Identifies recurrent winter vs summer tariff patterns.
iv.WHAT_PRETAX: Annual price change before taxes and VAT (energy commodity and network tariffs only).
iv.PURPOSE_PRETAX: Isolates market and network cost changes from government tax policy changes.
iv.WHAT_FINAL: Annual price change in final bill including all taxes, levies, and VAT.
iv.PURPOSE_FINAL: Evaluates overall consumer bill impact and determines whether fiscal tax intervention cushioned or amplified market price shocks.
iv.WHAT_EUR_RANK: Country rank based on nominal Euro prices.
iv.PURPOSE_EUR_RANK: Establishes raw nominal price hierarchy across Europe.
iv.WHAT_PPS_RANK: Country rank based on Purchasing Power Standards (PPS).
iv.PURPOSE_PPS_RANK: Measures national energy price affordability adjusted for general price levels.
iv.WHAT_RANK_SHIFT: Difference between nominal EUR rank and purchasing-power PPS rank.
iv.PURPOSE_RANK_SHIFT: Reveals whether energy prices are relatively more expensive or cheaper given national income levels.
iv.WHAT_DISPERSION: Percentage change in European price dispersion (Interquartile Range IQR) over 1 year.
iv.PURPOSE_DISPERSION: Measures whether European energy prices are converging or diverging across Member States.
iv.WHAT_BAND_PREMIUM: Percentage gap between selected consumption band price and baseline reference band price.
iv.PURPOSE_BAND_PREMIUM: Quantifies tariff volume discounting or premium for smaller/larger consumers.
iv.WHAT_BAND_PATTERN: Progression pattern of unit price across consumption volume bands (from low to high volume).
iv.PURPOSE_BAND_PATTERN: Reveals progressive vs volume-discounted tariff structures.
iv.WHAT_HICP_ENERGY: Annual YoY percentage change in focus country energy prices.
iv.PURPOSE_HICP_ENERGY: Tracks direct retail energy component of the consumer price index.
iv.WHAT_HICP_ALL: Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) annual inflation rate.
iv.PURPOSE_HICP_ALL: Measures general macroeconomic basket inflation across all goods and services.
iv.WHAT_INFLATION_GAP: Percentage point gap between energy YoY inflation and HICP general inflation.
iv.PURPOSE_INFLATION_GAP: Determines whether energy costs are driving up overall consumer inflation or buffering cost-of-living pressures.
iv.WHAT_PROVENANCE: Methodological reconciliation between bi-annual total prices and annual disaggregated component breakdowns.
iv.PURPOSE_PROVENANCE: Guides proper cross-referencing between bi-annual trend tracking and annual structural cost driver analysis.
iv.EXPLAIN_COUNTRY_COMPARISON: Bilateral price and component gap analysis between Focus Country A and selected Partner Country B.
iv.EXPLAIN_DEVELOPMENT: Advanced trend diagnostics including price momentum, multi-year compound growth (CAGR), volatility, and seasonal S1-to-S2 patterns.
iv.EXPLAIN_FISCAL: Analysis comparing pre-tax price movement vs final consumer price movement.
iv.EXPLAIN_EUROPE: Macro summary of price directions across European countries and Interquartile Range (IQR) dispersion.
iv.EXPLAIN_BAND: Price structure across volume consumption bands (from small to large consumers).
iv.EXPLAIN_HICP: Comparison between annual energy price inflation and HICP general consumer price inflation.
iv.EXPLAIN_PROVENANCE: Eurostat publication status flags, anomaly safeguards, dataset provenance IDs, and consumer methodology qualifications.
iv.IN_LINE_EU: broadly in line with the EU aggregate
iv.MIXED_MOVEMENT: No single component dominates the change
iv.NO_COMPONENT_DATA: Component breakdown is not available for this selection.
iv.FISCAL_CUSHIONED: Fiscal changes cushioned the underlying price increase
iv.FISCAL_AMPLIFIED: Fiscal changes amplified the underlying price increase
iv.FISCAL_OFFSET_DECREASE: Fiscal changes partly offset the underlying price decrease
iv.FISCAL_OPPOSITE_UP: The final price increased despite an underlying pre-tax decrease
iv.FISCAL_OPPOSITE_DOWN: The final price decreased despite an underlying pre-tax increase
iv.FISCAL_UNAVAILABLE: The fiscal effect could not be calculated for this selection.
iv.PPS_HIGHER: The price appears higher from a purchasing-power perspective
iv.PPS_LOWER: The price appears lower from a purchasing-power perspective
iv.PPS_SIMILAR: The purchasing-power position is broadly similar
iv.PPS_UNAVAILABLE: PPS comparison is not available for this selection.
iv.QUALITY_FOCUS_MISSING: No value is available for the selected geography and period.
iv.QUALITY_YOY_MISSING: No comparable value is available one year earlier.
iv.QUALITY_BENCHMARK_MISSING: The EU aggregate is not available for this selection.
iv.QUALITY_COMPONENT_MISSING: Component breakdown data is not available.
iv.QUALITY_INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY: Limited historical depth: fewer than 6 comparable observations.
iv.QUALITY_RECONCILIATION: Components do not fully reconcile with the total price; the breakdown is partial.
iv.QUALITY_OK: No data-quality issues were detected for this selection.
iv.EXPLAIN_LATEST_PRICE: The most recent available price for the product, consumer type, consumption band and geography selected above, including all taxes and levies.
iv.EXPLAIN_SEMESTER_CHANGE: Compares the latest price with the immediately preceding semester, for the same country and context.
iv.EXPLAIN_YOY_CHANGE: Compares the latest price with the same semester one year earlier, for the same country and context.
iv.EXPLAIN_EU_COMPARISON: Compares the selected country's price with the official EU27_2020 aggregate, for the same product, consumer type, band and period.
iv.EXPLAIN_COUNTRY_RANK: The country's position among all reporting countries with comparable data, ranked from highest to lowest price. EU and euro-area aggregates are excluded from the ranking.
iv.EXPLAIN_MEDIAN: Compares the country's price with the middle value of all reporting countries (not the official EU aggregate, which can differ from the median).
iv.EXPLAIN_HISTORICAL: Compares the latest price with the minimum, maximum and typical value of the full historical series available for this country and context.
iv.EXPLAIN_COMPOSITION: Breaks the final price down into its official components (energy and supply, network costs, taxes and levies) for the latest available year.
iv.EXPLAIN_MAIN_DRIVER: Identifies which price component changed the most, in price units, between the latest year and the previous year.
iv.EXPLAIN_FISCAL_EFFECT: Compares how much the pre-tax price changed with how much the final (all-taxes-included) price changed over the same year, to see whether taxation cushioned or amplified the movement.
iv.EXPLAIN_PPS: Recalculates the country's rank using Purchasing Power Standards instead of euro, to see whether the country's relative position changes once national price-level differences are accounted for. This is a purchasing-power perspective, not a direct measure of affordability.
iv.EXPLAIN_MOMENTUM: Compares the latest year-on-year change with the year-on-year change one semester earlier, to see whether the movement is accelerating, slowing, or reversing.
iv.EXPLAIN_CAGR: The smoothed annual growth rate over the selected number of years — not the actual change observed in each individual year.
iv.WHAT_LIFETIME_GROWTH: Calculates the total cumulative percentage change and multiplier from dataset inception to the latest period.
iv.WHAT_LONG_TERM_AVG: Compares the latest price with the arithmetic mean of all available historical semesters.
iv.WHAT_HISTORICAL_SPIKE: Identifies the single largest semestrial percentage price increase in the historical record.
iv.WHAT_HISTORICAL_DROP: Identifies the single largest semestrial percentage price decrease in the historical record.
iv.WHAT_CAGR_10Y: The 10-year compound annual growth rate across a full decade of semester price data.
iv.WHAT_HIGH_REGIME: Measures the proportion of historical semesters spent in the highest 20% price tier.
iv.COST_ESTIMATOR_DESC_HH: Enter your annual consumption (e.g. from your household utility bill) to estimate your yearly cost and find your Eurostat consumption band.
iv.COST_ESTIMATOR_DESC_NH: Enter your business's annual consumption (e.g. from energy statements) to estimate annual expenditure and identify your Eurostat consumption band.
iv.WHAT_CROSS_FUEL: Compares the cost per kWh of electricity against gas for the same consumer group.
iv.WHAT_CRISIS_RECOVERY: Tracks current price relative to the 2021–2023 Energy Crisis peak and 2019 pre-crisis baseline.
iv.WHAT_REGIONAL_RANK: Position of the focus country within its geographic region.
iv.PPS_EU_BASELINE_NOTE: PPS ranking benchmarks individual Member States against the EU baseline.
iv.COMPONENT_ANNUAL_NOTE: Note: Eurostat component breakdown datasets provide annual averages. Component shares are calculated relative to the annual average price.
iv.WHAT_AFFORDABILITY: Evaluates household and business purchasing power burden relative to national income levels.
iv.PURPOSE_AFFORDABILITY: Categorizes price level severity adjusted for purchasing power standard (PPS).
iv.EXPLAIN_VOLATILITY: The sample standard deviation of period-to-period percentage changes over the recent window — a higher value means more variable prices.
iv.EXPLAIN_SEASONAL: The typical difference between the first and second semester of the same year across the historical series, and whether the latest semester's movement was unusually large compared with that typical pattern.
iv.SEASONALLY_UNUSUAL: considerably larger than the typical seasonal movement
iv.SEASONALLY_TYPICAL: broadly in line with the typical seasonal movement
iv.EXPLAIN_RANK_SENSITIVITY: A country can move several ranking positions even when its own price barely changes, if neighbouring countries report very similar values. This checks the price gap to the country immediately above and below in the ranking.
iv.RANK_SENSITIVE: The exact rank is sensitive: neighbouring countries report very similar prices
iv.RANK_NOT_SENSITIVE: The rank is not sensitive to small price movements
iv.EXPLAIN_EUROPE_SNAPSHOT: How many comparable reporting countries saw prices rise, fall, or stay broadly stable over the last year, and whether the spread between countries is widening or narrowing.
iv.EXPLAIN_PERSISTENT_POSITION: Checks whether the country has consistently been in the highest- or lowest-price quartile over the last few years, rather than only in the current period.
iv.NOT_PERSISTENT: No persistent quartile pattern over the recent window
iv.EXPLAIN_BAND_PATTERN: Orders all available consumption bands from lowest to highest consumption to see whether the unit price rises, falls, or stays flat as consumption increases.
iv.PATTERN_MIXED: Mixed or irregular pattern across bands
iv.EXPLAIN_BAND_SPREAD: Tracks the price gap between the lowest and highest consumption bands from one year to the next, to see whether that gap is widening or narrowing.
iv.EXPLAIN_GLOBAL_COMPONENT: Compares the share of each component in the selected country's price with its share in the official EU aggregate's price, to see which component differs the most.
iv.EXPLAIN_INFLATION: Compares the energy price's annual change with the general consumer-price (HICP) annual rate of change for the same country, aligned to the last month of the semester. This is related context, not a cause-and-effect explanation of the energy-price movement.
iv.RELATED_CONTEXT_NOTE: Related context only — an association, not proof of cause and effect.
iv.PROVISIONAL: This is a provisional figure and may be revised.
iv.ANOMALY_NEGATIVE: The latest value is negative, which is unusual for this indicator — review before interpreting.
iv.ANOMALY_ZERO: The latest value is exactly zero, which may indicate a data issue.
iv.ANOMALY_IMPLAUSIBLE: The annual change is unusually large and may reflect a data break rather than a genuine price movement.
